sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca evaṃ vṛṣṇyandhakakule śrutvā mausalam āhavam pāṇḍavāḥ kim akurvanta tathā kṛṣṇe divaṃ gate
english: Janamejaya said: Having thus heard of the slaughter at the iron clubs among the houses of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, what did the Pāṇḍavas do when Kṛṣṇa too had gone to heaven?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śrutvaiva kauravo rājā vṛṣṇīnāṃ kadanaṃ mahat prasthāne matim ādhāya vākyam arjunam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The moment the Kaurava king heard of the great destruction of the Vṛṣṇis, he set his mind upon departure and spoke these words to Arjuna.

sanskrit: kālaḥ pacati bhūtāni sarvāṇy eva mahāmate karmanyāsam ahaṃ manye tvam api draṣṭum arhasi
english: Time ripens all created beings, O greatly wise one. I deem it fit that we lay down our deeds, and you too should recognize this.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tu kaunteyaḥ kālaḥ kāla iti bruvan anvapadyata tad vākyaṃ bhrātur jyeṣṭhasya vīryavān
english: So addressed, the valiant son of Kuntī, murmuring "Time, it is Time," assented to the words of his eldest brother.

sanskrit: arjunasya mataṃ jñātvā bhīmaseno yamau tathā anvapadyanta tad vākyaṃ yad uktaṃ savyasācinā
english: Learning Arjuna's resolve, Bhīmasena and the twins also assented to the words that Savyasācin had spoken.

sanskrit: tato yuyutsum ānāyya pravrajan dharmakāmyayā rājyaṃ paridadau sarvaṃ vaiśyāputre yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, summoning Yuyutsu and desiring to set forth in pursuit of dharma, made over the whole kingdom to that son born of a vaiśya woman.

sanskrit: abhiṣicya svarājye tu taṃ rājānaṃ parikṣitam duḥkhārtaś cābravīd rājā subhadrāṃ pāṇḍavāgrajaḥ
english: Having consecrated Parikṣit as king over his own realm, the eldest of the Pāṇḍavas, the king, sorely grieved, spoke to Subhadrā.

sanskrit: eṣa putrasya te putraḥ kururājo bhaviṣyati yadūnāṃ pariśeṣaś ca vajro rājā kṛtaś ca ha
english: This son of your son shall be the king of the Kurus; and Vajra, the survivor of the Yadus, has been made king.

sanskrit: parikṣid dhāstinapure śakraprasthe tu yādavaḥ vajro rājā tvayā rakṣyo mā cādharme manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: Parikṣit shall reign at Hāstinapura and the Yādava at Śakraprastha; Vajra the king is to be guarded by you. Set not your mind upon unrighteousness.

sanskrit: ity uktvā dharmarājaḥ sa vāsudevasya dhīmataḥ mātulasya ca vṛddhasya rāmādīnāṃ tathaiva ca
english: Having spoken thus, the Dharma King performed, for the wise Vāsudeva, for his aged maternal uncle, and likewise for Rāma and the others,

sanskrit: mātṛbhiḥ saha dharmātmā kṛtvodakam atandritaḥ śrāddhāny uddiśya sarveṣāṃ cakāra vidhivat tadā
english: together with the mothers, the righteous one, unwearied, offered the water-libations, and then duly performed the funerary rites in honour of them all.

sanskrit: dadau ratnāni vāsāṃsi grāmān aśvān rathān api striyaś ca dvijamukhyebhyo gavāṃ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: He gave to the foremost of the twice-born jewels, garments, villages, horses, chariots, and women, and cows by the hundreds of thousands.

sanskrit: kṛpam abhyarcya ca gurum arthamānapuraskṛtam śiṣyaṃ parikṣitaṃ tasmai dadau bharatasattamaḥ
english: Honouring the preceptor Kṛpa with wealth and high regard, the best of the Bharatas entrusted Parikṣit to him as his pupil.

sanskrit: tatas tu prakṛtīḥ sarvāḥ samānāyya yudhiṣṭhiraḥ sarvam ācaṣṭa rājarṣiś cikīrṣitam athātmanaḥ
english: Then the royal sage Yudhiṣṭhira, having assembled all his subjects, declared to them his whole intended purpose.

sanskrit: te śrutvaiva vacas tasya paurajānapadā janāḥ bhṛśam udvignamanaso nābhyanandanta tad vacaḥ
english: The people of the city and countryside, hearing his words, were sorely troubled in mind and did not welcome that speech.

sanskrit: naivaṃ kartavyam iti te tadocus te narādhipam na ca rājā tathākārṣīt kālaparyāyadharmavit
english: "This ought not to be done," they said then to the lord of men; but the king, who knew the law of the turning of Time, did not act otherwise.

sanskrit: tato 'numānya dharmātmā paurajānapadaṃ janam gamanāya matiṃ cakre bhrātaraś cāsya te tadā
english: Then the righteous one, having taken leave of the people of city and country, set his mind upon departure, and so too did his brothers.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā kauravyo dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ utsṛjyābharaṇāny aṅgāj jagṛhe valkalāny uta
english: Then that Kaurava king, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Dharma, casting the ornaments from his limbs, took up garments of bark.

sanskrit: bhīmārjunau yamau caiva draupadī ca yaśasvinī tathaiva sarve jagṛhur valkalāni janādhipa
english: Bhīma and Arjuna, the twins, and the illustrious Draupadī—all of them likewise took up the bark garments, O lord of men.

sanskrit: vidhivat kārayitveṣṭiṃ naiṣṭhikīṃ bharatarṣabha samutsṛjyāpsu sarve 'gnīn pratasthur narapuṃgavāḥ
english: Having duly performed the final sacrifice, O bull of the Bharatas, and cast their sacred fires into the waters, those bulls among men set forth.

sanskrit: tataḥ praruruduḥ sarvāḥ striyo dṛṣṭvā nararṣabhān prasthitān draupadīṣaṣṭhān purā dyūtajitān yathā
english: Then all the women wept aloud, seeing those bulls among men setting forth with Draupadī as the sixth, as of old when they had been beaten at the dice.

sanskrit: harṣo 'bhavac ca sarveṣāṃ bhrātṝṇāṃ gamanaṃ prati yudhiṣṭhiramataṃ jñātvā vṛṣṇikṣayam avekṣya ca
english: But joy arose in all the brothers at the prospect of departure, knowing Yudhiṣṭhira's resolve and beholding the destruction of the Vṛṣṇis.

sanskrit: bhrātaraḥ pañca kṛṣṇā ca ṣaṣṭhī śvā caiva saptamaḥ ātmanā saptamo rājā niryayau gajasāhvayāt paurair anugato dūraṃ sarvair antaḥpurais tathā
english: The five brothers, with Kṛṣṇā as the sixth and a dog as the seventh—the king himself thus the seventh—set out from the City named for the Elephant, followed far by the citizens and by all the women of the inner apartments.

sanskrit: na cainam aśakat kaś cin nivartasveti bhāṣitum nyavartanta tataḥ sarve narā nagaravāsinaḥ
english: None could bring himself to say to him, "Turn back"; and then all the men dwelling in the city returned.

sanskrit: kṛpaprabhṛtayaś caiva yuyutsuṃ paryavārayan viveśa gaṅgāṃ kauravya ulūpī bhujagātmajā
english: Kṛpa and the others gathered about Yuyutsu; and Ulūpī, the daughter of the serpent, entered the Gaṅgā, O Kaurava.

sanskrit: citrāṅgadā yayau cāpi maṇipūrapuraṃ prati śiṣṭāḥ parikṣitaṃ tv anyā mātaraḥ paryavārayan
english: Citrāṅgadā too went away towards the city of Maṇipūra, while the other mothers who remained gathered about Parikṣit.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś ca mahātmāno draupadī ca yaśasvinī kṛtopavāsāḥ kauravya prayayuḥ prāṅmukhās tataḥ
english: And the great-souled Pāṇḍavas and the illustrious Draupadī, having undertaken their fasts, O Kaurava, then set forth facing the east.

sanskrit: yogayuktā mahātmānas tyāgadharmam upeyuṣaḥ abhijagmur bahūn deśān saritaḥ parvatāṃs tathā
english: Yoked in yoga, those great-souled ones who had embraced the dharma of renunciation traversed many lands, rivers, and mountains.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro yayāv agre bhīmas tu tadanantaram arjunas tasya cānv eva yamau caiva yathākramam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira went in front, Bhīma next after him, Arjuna following him, and the twins in their order.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhatas tu varārohā śyāmā padmadalekṣaṇā draupadī yoṣitāṃ śreṣṭhā yayau bharatasattama
english: And behind them went Draupadī, the fair-hipped, dark-hued, lotus-petal-eyed, best of women, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: śvā caivānuyayāv ekaḥ pāṇḍavān prasthitān vane krameṇa te yayur vīrā lauhityaṃ salilārṇavam
english: And a single dog followed the Pāṇḍavas as they set forth into the forest. Step by step those heroes journeyed to the Lauhitya, the watery ocean.

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvaṃ ca dhanur divyaṃ na mumoca dhanaṃjayaḥ ratnalobhān mahārāja tau cākṣayyau maheṣudhī
english: Dhanaṃjaya did not relinquish the divine bow Gāṇḍīva, nor, out of attachment to those treasures, the two inexhaustible great quivers, O great king.

sanskrit: agniṃ te dadṛśus tatra sthitaṃ śailam ivāgrataḥ mārgam āvṛtya tiṣṭhantaṃ sākṣāt puruṣavigraham
english: There they beheld Agni standing before them like a mountain, barring their path, present in bodily human form.

sanskrit: tato devaḥ sa saptārciḥ pāṇḍavān idam abravīt bho bho pāṇḍusutā vīrāḥ pāvakaṃ māṃ vibodhata
english: Then that god of the seven flames spoke this to the Pāṇḍavas: "Ho, ho, heroic sons of Pāṇḍu! Know me to be Pāvaka, the Fire."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira mahābāho bhīmasena paraṃtapa arjunāśvisutau vīrau nibodhata vaco mama
english: "Mighty-armed Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīmasena scorcher of foes, Arjuna, and you two heroic sons of the Aśvins—heed my words."

sanskrit: aham agniḥ kuruśreṣṭhā mayā dagdhaṃ ca khāṇḍavam arjunasya prabhāveṇa tathā nārāyaṇasya ca
english: "I am Agni, O best of the Kurus, and by me was the Khāṇḍava forest consumed, through the might of Arjuna and likewise of Nārāyaṇa."

sanskrit: ayaṃ vaḥ phalguno bhrātā gāṇḍīvaṃ paramāyudham parityajya vanaṃ yātu nānenārtho 'sti kaś cana
english: "Let this your brother Phalguna give up the supreme weapon Gāṇḍīva and proceed into the forest; there is no longer any need of it."

sanskrit: cakraratnaṃ tu yat kṛṣṇe sthitam āsīn mahātmani gataṃ tac ca punar haste kālenaiṣyati tasya ha
english: "That jewel of a discus which rested in the hand of the great-souled Kṛṣṇa has departed, and in time it shall come again into his grasp."

sanskrit: varuṇād āhṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ mayaitat pārthakāraṇāt gāṇḍīvaṃ kārmukaśreṣṭhaṃ varuṇāyaiva dīyatām
english: "This Gāṇḍīva, best of bows, was formerly brought by me from Varuṇa for Pārtha's sake; let it now be given back to Varuṇa."

sanskrit: tatas te bhrātaraḥ sarve dhanaṃjayam acodayan sa jale prākṣipat tat tu tathākṣayyau maheṣudhī
english: Then all the brothers urged Dhanaṃjaya, and he cast into the water both the bow and the two inexhaustible great quivers.

sanskrit: tato 'gnir bharataśreṣṭha tatraivāntaradhīyata yayuś ca pāṇḍavā vīrās tatas te dakṣiṇāmukhāḥ
english: Then Agni, O best of the Bharatas, vanished on the very spot; and the heroic Pāṇḍavas went on thereafter, facing southward.

sanskrit: tatas te tūttareṇaiva tīreṇa lavaṇāmbhasaḥ jagmur bharataśārdūla diśaṃ dakṣiṇapaścimam
english: Then, along the northern shore of the salt sea, O tiger of the Bharatas, they journeyed towards the south-western quarter.

sanskrit: tataḥ punaḥ samāvṛttāḥ paścimāṃ diśam eva te dadṛśur dvārakāṃ cāpi sāgareṇa pariplutām
english: Then, turning again, they came to the western quarter, and there they saw Dvārakā engulfed by the ocean.

sanskrit: udīcīṃ punar āvṛttya yayur bharatasattamāḥ prādakṣiṇyaṃ cikīrṣantaḥ pṛthivyā yogadharmiṇaḥ
english: Turning once more to the north, those best of the Bharatas, devoted to the discipline of yoga, journeyed on, desiring to make their circumambulation of the earth.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas te niyatātmāna udīcīṃ diśam āsthitāḥ dadṛśur yogayuktāś ca himavantaṃ mahāgirim
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then those self-controlled ones, holding to the northern quarter and yoked in yoga, beheld the great mountain Himavat.

sanskrit: taṃ cāpy atikramantas te dadṛśur vālukārṇavam avaikṣanta mahāśailaṃ meruṃ śikhariṇāṃ varam
english: And as they crossed beyond it, they beheld a sea of sand, and they gazed upon the great mountain Meru, best of all peaks.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu gacchatāṃ śīghraṃ sarveṣāṃ yogadharmiṇām yājñasenī bhraṣṭayogā nipapāta mahītale
english: As all of them, devoted to the discipline of yoga, were going swiftly on, Yājñasenī, her yoga fallen away, dropped down upon the earth.

sanskrit: tāṃ tu prapatitāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ uvāca dharmarājānaṃ yājñasenīm avekṣya ha
english: Seeing her fallen, the mighty Bhīmasena, looking upon Yājñasenī, spoke to the Dharma King.

sanskrit: nādharmaś caritaḥ kaś cid rājaputryā paraṃtapa kāraṇaṃ kiṃ nu tad rājan yat kṛṣṇā patitā bhuvi
english: "No unrighteousness has been done by the princess, O scorcher of foes. What then is the cause, O king, that Kṛṣṇā has fallen to the ground?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pakṣapāto mahān asyā viśeṣeṇa dhanaṃjaye tasyaitat phalam adyaiṣā bhuṅkte puruṣasattama
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Great was her partiality, especially towards Dhanaṃjaya. The fruit of that she now reaps today, O best of men.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvānavekṣyaināṃ yayau dharmasuto nṛpaḥ samādhāya mano dhīmān dharmātmā puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, the king, the son of Dharma, went on without looking back at her—the wise, righteous bull among men, his mind firmly fixed.

sanskrit: sahadevas tato dhīmān nipapāta mahītale taṃ cāpi patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmo rājānam abravīt
english: Then the wise Sahadeva fell down upon the earth; and seeing him too fallen, Bhīma spoke to the king.

sanskrit: yo 'yam asmāsu sarveṣu śuśrūṣur anahaṃkṛtaḥ so 'yaṃ mādravatīputraḥ kasmān nipatito bhuvi
english: "He who was ever attentive in serving us all, and free of pride—this son of Mādravatī, why has he fallen to the ground?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ātmanaḥ sadṛśaṃ prājñaṃ naiṣo 'manyata kaṃ cana tena doṣeṇa patitas tasmād eṣa nṛpātmajaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: He thought none so wise as himself. By that fault has this prince fallen.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā tu samutsṛjya sahadevaṃ yayau tadā bhrātṛbhiḥ saha kaunteyaḥ śunā caiva yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus and left Sahadeva behind, the son of Kuntī, Yudhiṣṭhira, then went on together with his brothers and the dog.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇāṃ nipatitāṃ dṛṣṭvā sahadevaṃ ca pāṇḍavam ārto bandhupriyaḥ śūro nakulo nipapāta ha
english: Seeing Kṛṣṇā fallen and the Pāṇḍava Sahadeva likewise, the heroic Nakula, who loved his kinsmen, sank down stricken with grief.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite vīre nakule cārudarśane punar eva tadā bhīmo rājānam idam abravīt
english: When that hero Nakula of fair aspect had fallen, Bhīma once more spoke this to the king.

sanskrit: yo 'yam akṣatadharmātmā bhrātā vacanakārakaḥ rūpeṇāpratimo loke nakulaḥ patito bhuvi
english: "This brother of unblemished righteousness, ever obedient to our word, unmatched in beauty in the world—Nakula has fallen to the ground."

sanskrit: ity ukto bhīmasenena pratyuvāca yudhiṣṭhiraḥ nakulaṃ prati dharmātmā sarvabuddhimatāṃ varaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Bhīmasena, the righteous Yudhiṣṭhira, best of all the wise, replied concerning Nakula.

sanskrit: rūpeṇa matsamo nāsti kaś cid ity asya darśanam adhikaś cāham evaika ity asya manasi sthitam
english: "'In beauty none is equal to me'—such was his view; and 'I alone am surpassing'—this stood fixed in his mind."

sanskrit: nakulaḥ patitas tasmād āgaccha tvaṃ vṛkodara yasya yad vihitaṃ vīra so 'vaśyaṃ tad upāśnute
english: "For that reason has Nakula fallen. Come on, O Vṛkodara. Whatever is ordained for a man, that he must surely undergo, O hero."

sanskrit: tāṃs tu prapatitān dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavaḥ śvetavāhanaḥ papāta śokasaṃtaptas tato 'nu paravīrahā
english: Seeing them fallen, the Pāṇḍava of the white steeds, the slayer of hostile heroes, then in his turn sank down, consumed with grief.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu puruṣavyāghre patite śakratejasi mriyamāṇe durādharṣe bhīmo rājānam abravīt
english: When that tiger among men, of Indra's splendour, the unassailable one, had fallen and lay dying, Bhīma spoke to the king.

sanskrit: anṛtaṃ na smarāmy asya svaireṣv api mahātmanaḥ atha kasya vikāro 'yaṃ yenāyaṃ patito bhuvi
english: "I do not recall a single falsehood of this great-souled one, not even in jest. What then is the fault by which he has fallen to the ground?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ekāhnā nirdaheyaṃ vai śatrūn ity arjuno 'bravīt na ca tat kṛtavān eṣa śūramānī tato 'patat
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "In a single day I shall burn up my foes," so Arjuna said; yet he did not accomplish it. Proud of his prowess, he therefore fell.

sanskrit: avamene dhanur grāhān eṣa sarvāṃś ca phalgunaḥ yathā coktaṃ tathā caiva kartavyaṃ bhūtim icchatā
english: And this Phalguna held in contempt all other bowmen. One who desires prosperity should do even as he has said.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā prasthito rājā bhīmo 'tha nipapāta ha patitaś cābravīd bhīmo dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, the king went on; and then Bhīma fell down. Fallen, Bhīma spoke to the Dharma King Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: bho bho rājann avekṣasva patito 'haṃ priyas tava kiṃnimittaṃ ca patanaṃ brūhi me yadi vettha ha
english: "Ho, ho, O king! Look back—I, your beloved, have fallen. And tell me the cause of my fall, if you know it."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca atibhuktaṃ ca bhavatā prāṇena ca vikatthase anavekṣya paraṃ pārtha tenāsi patitaḥ kṣitau
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: You ate to excess, and you boasted of your strength; and you took no heed of others, O Pārtha. For that you have fallen to the earth.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā taṃ mahābāhur jagāmānavalokayan śvā tv eko 'nuyayau yas te bahuśaḥ kīrtito mayā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus to him, the mighty-armed one went on without looking back; and only the dog followed him—that dog whom I have so often mentioned to you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ saṃnādayañ śakro divaṃ bhūmiṃ ca sarvaśaḥ rathenopayayau pārtham ārohety abravīc ca tam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Śakra, making heaven and earth resound on every side, came near to Pārtha with his chariot and said to him, "Mount up."

sanskrit: sa bhrātṝn patitān dṛṣṭvā dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ abravīc chokasaṃtaptaḥ sahasrākṣam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Seeing his brothers fallen, the Dharma King Yudhiṣṭhira, consumed with grief, spoke this word to the Thousand-eyed one.

sanskrit: bhrātaraḥ patitā me 'tra āgaccheyur mayā saha na vinā bhrātṛbhiḥ svargam icche gantuṃ sureśvara
english: "My brothers have fallen here; let them come with me. Without my brothers I do not wish to go to heaven, O lord of the gods."

sanskrit: sukumārī sukhārhā ca rājaputrī puraṃdara sāsmābhiḥ saha gaccheta tad bhavān anumanyatām
english: "The princess too, so delicate and worthy of every comfort, O Purandara—let her come with us; may you grant this."

sanskrit: indra uvāca bhrātṝn drakṣyasi putrāṃs tvam agratas tridivaṃ gatān kṛṣṇayā sahitān sarvān mā śuco bharatarṣabha
english: Indra said: Your brothers and your sons, who have gone before to the third heaven, you shall behold—all of them, together with Kṛṣṇā. Grieve not, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: nikṣipya mānuṣaṃ dehaṃ gatās te bharatarṣabha anena tvaṃ śarīreṇa svargaṃ gantā na saṃśayaḥ
english: Having laid aside their human bodies, they have gone there, O bull of the Bharatas; but you shall go to heaven in this very body—of that there is no doubt.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ayaṃ śvā bhūtabhavyeśa bhakto māṃ nityam eva ha sa gaccheta mayā sārdham ānṛśaṃsyā hi me matiḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: This dog, O lord of what is and what shall be, has been devoted to me always. Let him go along with me, for my mind is set on freedom from cruelty.

sanskrit: indra uvāca amartyatvaṃ matsamatvaṃ ca rājañ; śriyaṃ kṛtsnāṃ mahatīṃ caiva kīrtim saṃprāpto 'dya svargasukhāni ca tvaṃ; tyaja śvānaṃ nātra nṛśaṃsam asti
english: Indra said: Immortality and equality with myself, O king, and prosperity entire and vast, and renown, and the joys of heaven you have now attained today. Abandon the dog; in this there is no cruelty.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca anāryam āryeṇa sahasranetra; śakyaṃ kartuṃ duṣkaram etad ārya mā me śriyā saṃgamanaṃ tayāstu; yasyāḥ kṛte bhaktajanaṃ tyajeyam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: An ignoble deed is hard for a noble man to do, O thousand-eyed and noble one. Let me have no union with that prosperity for whose sake I must forsake one who is devoted to me.

sanskrit: indra uvāca svarge loke śvavatāṃ nāsti dhiṣṇyam; iṣṭāpūrtaṃ krodhavaśā haranti tato vicārya kriyatāṃ dharmarāja; tyaja śvānaṃ nātra nṛśaṃsam asti
english: Indra said: In the world of heaven there is no abode for those who keep a dog; the Krodhavaśas carry off the merit of sacrifice and pious works. Therefore, having considered, do as is fitting, O Dharma King: abandon the dog; in this there is no cruelty.
